wrong.note: While oxygen is electronegative, you only considered the $-I$ effect. In aromatic rings, the resonance ($+R$) effect of the oxygen lone pair is stronger and pushes electrons into the ring.

recap.key_idea: When a group like $-OCH_3$ is attached to a benzene ring, the resonance ($+R$) effect of its lone pairs usually outweighs its inductive ($-I$) effect, making the ring more reactive and directing substitutions to the $o/p$ positions.
